subject: Pilot telemetry onboarding & evaluation timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@brightlinehealth.com>, Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot telemetry onboarding & evaluation timeline

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps for the pilot so we can align on scope, success criteria, and owners.

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: Validate production-grade retrieval + generation pipeline for patient-facing summaries (no PHI in test data).
- Key constraints: no PHI in exported logs; Splunk ingestion for logs; 90-day retention; must meet latency/cost targets.

Proposed pilot scope (2-week technical validation):
1) Baseline week (run your sample traffic against our hosted trial model): measure p95 latency, error rate, token cost.
2) Optimization week (apply batching, KV-cache suggestions, and a deduped embedding index) and re-run the eval harness.

Success criteria (please confirm):
- p95 latency < 250ms for generation ops under 512-token prompts
- API error rate < 0.5%
- Embedding recall (top-10) >= 0.87 on your representative queries
- Logs exported to your Splunk instance with sensitive fields redacted

Owners (tentative):
- Soojin (pilot PM / coordination) — I'll run the schedule and syncs
- Ben (infra & deployment) — sets up trial endpoints / dedicated pool if required
- Laura (observability / dashboards) — dashboard templates, alerts, and trace instrumentation

Deliverables I'll share this afternoon: redwood-poc-outline.pdf and a metrics template (rbw-poc-metrics-template.csv).
Proposed timeline: Dec 10 kickoff (handshake + environment access), validation weeks Dec 13–24, wrap and decision meeting Jan 3. Open to adjusting to your calendar.

Action items for Brightline:
- Confirm success criteria above or add changes
- Confirm whether sample traffic can be anonymized and shared for load testing
- Provide Splunk ingestion endpoint details (or confirm we can push to S3 for your ingestion team)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite and the attachments now.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nisha Patel <nisha.patel@brightlinehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot telemetry onboarding & evaluation timeline

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming Brightline's inputs and a couple of constraints so we land on a feasible plan.

Confirmed success criteria (slightly modified):
- p95 latency < 250ms for generation under 512 tokens (we can accept 300ms for first 48 hours while you fine-tune batching)
- API error rate target < 0.5%
- Embedding recall >= 0.87 for our anonymized test set (we’ll provide the queries)
- Observability: traces with request id, token counts, and model variant logged.

Non-negotiables / constraints:
- No PHI may leave Brightline systems — test corpus will be fully anonymized and scoped by our compliance team
- Logs must be delivered to our Splunk instance behind the company VPC; if S3 staging is easier, we need a signed transfer with encryption and receipt confirmation

Timeline tweak: internal approvals push our kickoff to Jan 10, 2028; can run Jan 10–Jan 24 for the 2-week run + Jan 25 buffer for exports and report.

Open asks for Redwood: 
- Security checklist and SOC2 evidence stub (NDA already signed)
- Short list of the observability metrics you’ll populate (traces, dashboards, alert rules)

On the attachment: I can see the outline you referenced. Please also include a field-level redaction approach so our compliance folks sign off quickly.

Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 07:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot telemetry onboarding & evaluation timeline — updated plan & owners

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the timeline update. Per your asks, I’m attaching the POC outline and metrics template; below is the refined onboarding & eval plan incorporating Splunk ingestion and compliance constraints.

POC / onboarding highlights (final draft):
- Kickoff: Jan 10, 2028 — handshake call to confirm access and anonymized dataset delivery
- Week 1 (Jan 11–17): Baseline run using anonymized traffic profile; collect metrics and trace spans
- Week 2 (Jan 18–24): Apply optimization levers (batching, cache configs, quantization profile if applicable); re-run evaluation
- Post-run (Jan 25–31): Export logs, verify ingestion, and deliver the evaluation report + dashboards

Observability deliverables (Laura owner):
- Pre-built dashboards: Request throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, API errors, token throughput, model-variant distribution, KV cache hit rate
- Trace spans: request.start, request.encode, model.latency, kv.cache.lookup — include request_id and user_anonymized_id (no PII)
- Alert rules: p95 > 300ms (warn) / > 400ms (critical); error rate > 0.5% (critical); failed export jobs > 0 in 24h
- Log export: Redwood will stage logs to an encrypted S3 bucket and provide signed links for Brightline to ingest into Splunk; retention control set to 90 days by default

Evaluation plan (metrics & acceptance):
- Latency: p95 generation < 250ms (target) with documented tuning steps if we start at higher numbers
- Reliability: API error rate < 0.5% during baseline and optimization runs
- Embedding recall: >= 0.87 top-10 lookup on your anonymized eval set
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens baseline vs post-optimizations (for your procurement visibility)

Owners (final):
- Soojin Lee — pilot PM, stakeholder coordination, scheduling
- Ben Carter — infra + trial endpoint config, S3/log staging, and access controls
- Laura Bennett — dashboards, trace instrumentation, alert rules, post-run report

Next steps (for Jan 10 kickoff):
1) Brightline to confirm anonymized dataset delivery method and give an approximate sample size (QPS / daily volume)
2) Brightline to share Splunk ingestion details or confirm S3 staging is acceptable
3) Redwood to share security stub and redaction approach (attached in pdf)
4) I’ll send calendar invites for Jan 10 kickoff + weekly syncs during the pilot

Attachments: redwood-poc-outline.pdf, rbw-poc-metrics-template.csv

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot telemetry onboarding & evaluation timeline — infra notes

Quick confirmation from infra side: we can provision a trial endpoint and a short-lived encrypted S3 bucket for log staging. A couple of operational items I need from Brightline before Jan 10:
- A test service account (least privilege) for S3 write or the Splunk HEC token if you prefer direct push
- Approx QPS and median request size so I can size the instance and quantify expected token throughput
- Any IP allowlists for the VPC egress (if pushing directly to Splunk)

I'll coordinate firewall/allowlist windows with your network team during the kickoff. Once we have the above, I’ll provision the endpoint and share endpoint creds via our secure vault and confirm the dashboard wiring with Laura.
